title: The Chandogya Upanishad, with Shankara's commentary
attributionNote: Anonymous, and — like the other Vedic Upanishads — transmitted as the teaching of several named teachers, Uddalaka Aruni above all. The commentary beside the text is ascribed to Shankara.
description: The Chandogya teaches the identity of the self with the ground of the world through the analogy of salt dissolved in water and through the instruction of Uddalaka to his son Shvetaketu: that thou art. Beside those verses it carries the oldest Indian account of the states of the self, the chant of the udgitha, the story of Satyakama the truthful and the doctrine of the five fires.
historicalContext: Historically one of the first Upanishads to be translated into a European language, and the Upanishad that gave the nineteenth-century West the sentence tat tvam asi. In the Vedanta schools Shankara's commentary is the reading against which the other commentaries define themselves.
availabilityNote: Complete: the eight adhyayas and 154 khandas of the GRETIL e-text, streamed at read time one khanda at a time, with the commentary ascribed to Shankara in a second pane.
